rules.title: Avoid sync-over-async
rules.summary: Await asynchronous work instead of blocking with Result, Wait, or GetAwaiter().GetResult().
rules.rationale: Blocking a Task ties up a thread and can starve the thread pool under load. In request code it also defeats end-to-end asynchrony.

rules.title: Do not call Thread.Sleep from asynchronous code
rules.summary: Use an awaited delay or another non-blocking coordination primitive.
rules.rationale: Thread.Sleep occupies the current worker for the full delay. Task.Delay yields the worker and supports cancellation.

rules.title: Avoid async void outside event handlers
rules.summary: Return Task or ValueTask so callers can await completion and observe exceptions.
rules.rationale: Exceptions from async void cannot be observed through a returned task, and callers cannot compose or cancel the operation.
rules.bad: public async void RefreshAsync() => await RefreshCoreAsync();
rules.good: public async Task RefreshAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken) => await RefreshCoreAsync(cancellationToken);

rules.title: Forward the available CancellationToken
rules.summary: Pass the current operation's token to cancellable asynchronous calls.
rules.rationale: Dropping a token lets downstream I/O continue after a request, job, or caller has been cancelled.

rules.title: Do not replace an available token with CancellationToken.None
rules.summary: Use the token already available in the current operation.
rules.rationale: CancellationToken.None silently breaks cancellation propagation and wastes work after abandonment.

rules.title: Avoid string accumulation in loops
rules.summary: Use StringBuilder, a buffer, string.Create, or a single join operation for repeated concatenation.
rules.rationale: Strings are immutable. Repeated accumulation copies the growing string and creates many temporary objects.
rules.bad: foreach (var item in items) text += item.Name;
rules.good: var builder = new StringBuilder(capacity); foreach (var item in items) builder.Append(item.Name);

rules.title: Use Any for an existence check
rules.summary: Do not enumerate a LINQ sequence with Count or LongCount only to compare the result with zero.
rules.rationale: Any can stop at the first element and translates to an existence query for LINQ providers.

rules.title: Avoid repeated enumeration of a lazy sequence
rules.summary: Materialize once or restructure the operation when the same lazy sequence is enumerated repeatedly.
rules.rationale: Repeated enumeration can repeat expensive work, consume one-shot iterators, or execute a database query more than once.
rules.good: var materialized = orders.ToList(); if (materialized.Count != 0) return materialized;

rules.title: Set collection capacity when the size is knowable
rules.summary: Provide an initial capacity when a collection is populated from a source with a known count.
rules.rationale: Capacity hints avoid repeated array growth, copying, and temporary allocations.
rules.bad: var result = new List<Order>(); foreach (var order in orders) result.Add(Map(order));
rules.good: var result = new List<Order>(orders.Count); foreach (var order in orders) result.Add(Map(order));

rules.title: Avoid boxing in hot loops
rules.summary: Keep value types on generic or strongly typed paths inside loops.
rules.rationale: Converting a value type to object or an interface can allocate a boxed copy on the managed heap.

rules.title: Consume a ValueTask only once
rules.summary: Await a ValueTask once, or convert it to a Task once when repeated consumption is required.
rules.rationale: A ValueTask may wrap an IValueTaskSource and is not generally safe to await, inspect, or convert multiple times.
rules.good: var task = pending.AsTask(); await task; await task;

rules.title: Bound asynchronous fan-out
rules.summary: Do not feed an unbounded projection directly into Task.WhenAll.
rules.rationale: Starting one operation per input can exhaust sockets, database pools, memory, or downstream rate limits.
rules.good: await Parallel.ForEachAsync(ids, new ParallelOptions { MaxDegreeOfParallelism = 16, CancellationToken = cancellationToken }, LoadAsync);

rules.title: Run TaskCompletionSource continuations asynchronously
rules.summary: Create TaskCompletionSource with TaskCreationOptions.RunContinuationsAsynchronously.
rules.rationale: Running continuations inline on the thread that completes the source can couple unrelated components, block the producer, or deadlock code that holds a lock.

rules.title: Do not convert async lambdas to void-returning delegates
rules.summary: Use a Task-returning delegate so completion and exceptions remain observable.
rules.rationale: An async lambda converted to a void-returning delegate has async-void semantics: callers cannot await it or observe its completion and exceptions through a returned task.

rules.title: Do not silently swallow exceptions
rules.summary: Handle, propagate, or document the intentional swallowing of a specific exception.
rules.rationale: An empty catch can hide failed work and corrupt control flow without leaving evidence for callers or operators.
rules.good: try { Save(); } catch (OperationCanceledException) { /* Expected after caller cancellation. */ }

rules.title: Do not build a nested service provider
rules.summary: Let the host build and own the application service provider.
rules.rationale: BuildServiceProvider during registration creates duplicate singleton graphs, broken scopes, and disposal leaks.

rules.title: Do not register DbContext as a singleton
rules.summary: Use AddDbContext or a scoped registration for DbContext.
rules.rationale: DbContext is not thread-safe and is designed around a short unit-of-work lifetime.

rules.title: Do not capture a scoped dependency in a singleton
rules.summary: Redesign the lifetime boundary or create an explicit scope at operation time.
rules.rationale: A singleton that holds a scoped service effectively promotes it to the root lifetime and can use disposed or non-thread-safe state.
rules.good: services.AddSingleton<ReportCache>(); // ReportCache(IServiceScopeFactory scopes), resolve per operation

rules.title: Request handlers should accept CancellationToken
rules.summary: Accept the request-aborted token in asynchronous controllers, minimal API handlers, and middleware delegates.
rules.rationale: ASP.NET Core binds CancellationToken to HttpContext.RequestAborted, allowing disconnected requests to stop downstream work.

rules.title: Do not construct HttpClient per request
rules.summary: Inject HttpClient, use a typed client, or use IHttpClientFactory.
rules.rationale: Per-operation clients lose handler pooling and can cause connection churn or socket exhaustion.
rules.bad: var client = new HttpClient(); return await client.GetStringAsync(uri);

rules.title: Guard development-only middleware
rules.summary: Place developer exception pages, migration endpoints, and interactive API UI behind an environment or explicit security guard.
rules.rationale: Development diagnostics can expose implementation details and unnecessarily expand a production attack surface.

rules.title: Do not fire-and-forget request work
rules.summary: Await request work or enqueue a durable/background operation that owns its scope.
rules.rationale: Unobserved request tasks can outlive scoped services, lose exceptions, and disappear when the process shuts down.
rules.good: app.MapPost("/jobs", async (Job job, CancellationToken ct) => { await queue.EnqueueAsync(job, ct); return Results.Accepted(); });

rules.title: Do not cache IHttpContextAccessor.HttpContext
rules.summary: Store IHttpContextAccessor and read its current HttpContext when needed.
rules.rationale: A captured HttpContext can be null during construction or refer to a request that is no longer current when the stored value is read.

rules.title: Validate bound options at startup
rules.summary: Call ValidateOnStart after binding options so invalid configuration fails during startup.
rules.rationale: Deferred options validation lets invalid configuration survive deployment and fail only when the affected feature is first used.

rules.title: Observe EventCallback.InvokeAsync tasks
rules.summary: Await, return, or otherwise observe the Task returned by EventCallback.InvokeAsync.
rules.rationale: Dropping an EventCallback task hides callback failures and allows the initiating component to continue before the parent callback completes.

rules.title: Use no-tracking for read-only entity queries
rules.summary: Add AsNoTracking or configure no-tracking behavior when entities are materialized only for reading.
rules.rationale: Change tracking adds identity-map work and retained state that read-only paths do not need.

rules.title: Do not re-enable tracking on a read-only query
rules.summary: Remove AsTracking from read-only query chains, especially after AsNoTracking.
rules.rationale: AsTracking overrides no-tracking behavior and reintroduces state management costs.

rules.title: Pass CancellationToken to EF Core async queries
rules.summary: Supply the current token to EF Core asynchronous terminal operators.
rules.rationale: Database commands can continue consuming a connection and server resources after the caller has gone away.

rules.title: Pass CancellationToken to SaveChangesAsync
rules.summary: Supply the current token when persisting changes.
rules.rationale: SaveChangesAsync may perform multiple database commands and should participate in request or job cancellation.

rules.title: Avoid database queries inside loops
rules.summary: Batch keys, join, project, or prefetch instead of issuing one query per iteration.
rules.rationale: A query in a loop commonly creates an N+1 round-trip pattern whose latency grows with input size.
rules.bad: foreach (var id in ids) orders.Add(await db.Orders.SingleAsync(x => x.Id == id, ct));

rules.title: Keep filtering and projection on the server
rules.summary: Apply Where, Select, ordering, and paging before materialization.
rules.rationale: Materializing before shaping transfers extra rows and columns and spends CPU and memory in the application.
rules.good: await db.Orders.Where(x => x.Status == Status.Open).Select(x => new OrderDto(x.Id)).ToListAsync(ct);

rules.title: Parameterize raw SQL
rules.summary: Use interpolated EF APIs or explicit parameters rather than composing user or variable data into Raw SQL APIs.
rules.rationale: Dynamic text passed to Raw APIs can change SQL structure and introduce injection vulnerabilities.

rules.title: Bound request-driven query materialization
rules.summary: Page, cap, stream, or aggregate entity collections returned from request handlers.
rules.rationale: An unbounded ToListAsync can turn data growth into high latency, large allocations, and response failures.
rules.bad: app.MapGet("/orders", async (AppDbContext db, CancellationToken ct) => await db.Orders.AsNoTracking().ToListAsync(ct));
rules.good: app.MapGet("/orders", async (int skip, AppDbContext db, CancellationToken ct) => await db.Orders.AsNoTracking().OrderBy(x => x.Id).Skip(skip).Take(100).ToListAsync(ct));

rules.title: Use AnyAsync for existence checks
rules.summary: Use AnyAsync rather than comparing CountAsync with zero.
rules.rationale: An existence query can stop when a match is found and normally translates to EXISTS.

rules.title: Do not run parallel operations on one DbContext
rules.summary: Await each operation before starting the next, or give concurrent operations separate scopes and DbContext instances.
rules.rationale: DbContext does not support multiple parallel operations and can corrupt unit-of-work assumptions.
rules.good: var orders = await db.Orders.ToListAsync(ct); var customers = await db.Customers.ToListAsync(ct);

rules.title: Asynchronous tests must return Task
rules.summary: Use Task or ValueTask for asynchronous test methods; never async void.
rules.rationale: Test runners cannot reliably await async void tests or associate later exceptions with the correct test.
rules.bad: [Fact] public async void Saves_order() { await Sut.SaveAsync(); }
rules.good: [Fact] public async Task Saves_order() { await Sut.SaveAsync(); }
